body:
Docker CPU limits applied after launch were ignored, so a 4-CPU workload on a 6-CPU daemon could never reach the default 95% trigger, and a penalty lift restored 6 instead of 4. A dead monitor could also leave its 2-CPU cap in place because the watcher never restarted it and zombie/reused-PID locks blocked reattachment.

This change inspects the current quota on each tick, remembers the pre-penalty base across restarts and resume, and restores the lower of that base and current daemon capacity. A different supervisor quota becomes the new base. Watchers now supervise and reap monitors; Linux locks distinguish zombies and process birth identity, and transient tick failures discard coverage and retry. Graceful stop restores an owned cap on the same attempt. JavaScript and Rust use matching policy, adapter and shared-contract evidence. Transition logs identify the window and phase denominator; opt-in debug tracing explains failures and measured capacity.

Both child issues reproduced on the original source; neither is deferred or treated as already resolved.

- [Every requirement, alternatives and implementation plan](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/blob/issue-207-c95cbdc7bbc2/docs/case-studies/issue-207/requirements.md)
- [Root causes and primary-source component research](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/blob/issue-207-c95cbdc7bbc2/docs/case-studies/issue-207/research.md): Docker/Linux documentation, proper-lockfile, dockerode, Bollard and Tini.
- [Reproduction commands and preserved raw evidence](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/blob/issue-207-c95cbdc7bbc2/docs/case-studies/issue-207/validation.md)
- [CI investigation with all failed-job logs and their correction](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/blob/issue-207-c95cbdc7bbc2/docs/case-studies/issue-207/ci.md)

Validation:

- `cd js && bun run check && bun run test`: 1,220 passed, zero failed.
- Shared golden/CI guard tests: 35 passed; feature inventory, workflow gating, pinned executable Rust regeneration and Rust formatting passed.
- The new regressions failed before implementation and now cover NanoCPU/legacy quotas, saved base and JSON status, restarted monitors, zombie/reused-PID locks, a killed supervised child, publication failure, graceful restoration, supervisor overrides, daemon-clamped restart and lock ownership after inode reuse.
- Real Docker acceptance: post-launch `--cpus 4` → default 95% trigger → 2-CPU penalty → kill watcher/supervisor/monitor → real `--resume-all` → idle release to 4; verified HostConfig and JSON status. Run `python3 examples/issue-207-cpu-recovery.py` after pulling `alpine:3.23`.
- [Same-commit CI](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/actions/runs/38140966575) passes on `6118e5a`: JavaScript and Rust tests on Linux/macOS/Windows, both required stages, lint, shared contracts, generation, audits and Rust CodeQL. Rust coverage is 71.76%.
- [Security](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/actions/runs/38140966423) and [broken-link checks](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/actions/runs/38140966544) pass on the same commit. Current main is an ancestor; the worktree is clean.

SIGKILL requires surviving supervision or explicit reattachment; an indefinite Docker outage prevents quota updates. No new runtime dependency is needed. JavaScript changeset and Rust changelog fragments prepare patch releases.

Fixes #205
Fixes #206
Fixes #207
title: fix: restore observed CPU quotas and recover penalty monitors
